tapping-shoulder.context: A hand tapping the shoulder of a person seen from behind. Used for getting someone's attention, nudges and reminders, and polite interruptions in social or workplace apps.

walking-bicycle.context: A person walking beside a bicycle while holding its handlebar. Used for dismount zones, bike parking areas, pedestrian-only paths and routes where cyclists must walk.

reading-map.context: A standing person holding up a large unfolded paper map. Used for tourist information, navigation and wayfinding, travel guides and orienteering.

looking-in-fridge.context: A person bending toward an open refrigerator to look inside. Used for snack and hunger moments, meal planning, food inventory and kitchen or home apps.

tidying-toys.context: A child dropping a toy block into a toy box that already holds a teddy bear. Used for chores charts, tidy-up time, parenting and nursery or classroom routines.

blowing-up-balloon.context: A face in profile with a puffed cheek blowing air into a balloon. Used for party preparation, birthdays, celebrations and decoration tasks.

recording-voice-message.context: A person holding a phone near their mouth with sound going into it. Used for voice notes, voice messages in chat apps, dictation and audio recording features.

sign-language-thank-you.context: A flat hand moving forward and down from the chin, as in the sign for thank you. Used for sign language learning, accessibility content, deaf awareness and gratitude messages.

sign-language-please.context: A flat palm held on the chest with a circling arrow, as in the sign for please. Used for sign language lessons, baby sign, accessibility content and polite requests.

sign-language-help.context: A thumbs-up fist resting on a flat palm with an upward arrow, as in the sign for help. Used for sign language learning, accessibility services, support desks and assistance requests.

fist-pump.context: A person pulling a clenched fist down in celebration. Used for wins, goals reached, achievements, streaks and success messages.

stomping.context: A person stamping one foot down hard with impact lines at the heel. Used for anger and frustration, marching, stamping out and loud footsteps.

toddler-tantrum.context: A small child lying on its back kicking its legs and waving its fists. Used for parenting apps, child behaviour and development content, and meltdown moments.

pacing.context: A walking person above a curved arrow pointing both ways, showing a back-and-forth path. Used for restlessness, nervous waiting, anxiety and thinking on the move.

biting-nails.context: A worried face with fingertips held between the teeth. Used for nervousness, suspense, anxiety and waiting on results.

pushing-car.context: A person leaning forward and pushing a small car from behind. Used for breakdowns, stalled vehicles, flat batteries, running out of fuel and roadside help.

arm-in-arm.context: Two people walking side by side with their elbows linked. Used for friendship, couples, companionship, support and walking together.

taping-box.context: A tape roll on top of a closed cardboard box with its top seam taped. Used for packing, moving house, shipping parcels and preparing orders.

handing-over-keys.context: One hand passing a key to another open hand. Used for key handover, new homes, rentals and move-in day, car hire and check-in.

opening-jar.context: A jar with its lid twisting off and a curved arrow. Used for opening instructions, twist-off lids, food storage, kitchen tasks and grip strength.

climbing-tree.context: A person hugging the trunk of a leafy tree while climbing it. Used for outdoor play, childhood activities, adventure, nature and treehouse content.

carrying-firewood.context: A person carrying a stack of round logs in both arms. Used for firewood and fireplace content, cabins and camping, heating and winter chores.

giving-up-seat.context: A standing person gesturing toward an empty seat as an older person with a cane approaches. Used for priority seating, courtesy on public transport and kindness campaigns.

beating-rug.context: A person swinging a carpet beater at a rug hanging over a line, with dust flying. Used for spring cleaning, household chores, dust removal and carpet care.

pumping-tire.context: A floor pump with its hose connected to a bicycle wheel. Used for tyre inflation, bike maintenance, repair shops and flat tyre help.

scraping-windshield.context: An ice scraper clearing a stripe across a frosted car windshield. Used for winter driving tips, frost warnings, car care and cold weather preparation.

sign-language-yes.context: An upright fist nodding forward at the wrist with motion arcs, as in the sign for yes. Used for sign language learning, accessibility content and agreement.

sign-language-no.context: A hand with the index and middle fingers closing onto the thumb, with a small arrow, as in the sign for no. Used for sign language learning, accessibility content and refusals.
